title: Burst safety margin for new model entrance
summary: Working capacity worksheet estimating GPU and KV cache headroom needed to safely admit a new generation model into production across regions. Includes three ramp scenarios, per-region impact, rough GPU-equivalent estimates, and mitigations (seeding, soft quotas, routing).
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a working estimate for the extra capacity (GPU and KV cache memory) we need to provision or reserve to safely onboard a new higher-context model into hosted and dedicated fleets without violating latency SLOs or causing eviction storms in KV caches. It is intentionally conservative in some inputs to surface risk.

Key outcomes (preview):
- Nominal scenario: +18% KV memory pressure globally, equivalent to ~42 A100-80GB GPU warm slots (regional distribution required).
- Conservative (fast ramp): +35% KV pressure, ~90 GPU warm slots; requires immediate seeding + short-term burst capacity.
- Aggressive (viral adoption): +60% KV pressure, ~160 GPU warm slots; mitigation: blocklist non-critical routes, strict soft-quota, and expedited autoscale.

Assumptions (editable):
- Current active fleets (prod): us-west1: 420 A100 slots (68% avg util), us-east1: 330 A100 slots (62% util), eu-west1: 210 A100 slots (57% util), apac-sg1: 120 H100 slots (61% util).
- Baseline KV cache occupancy: 12 TB global (prefix and session KV combined).
- Baseline median request tokens: 64 input, 128 output. New model expected median output tokens: 220 (longer completions).
- Average KV per token (after compression/packing): 35 bytes/token of KV metadata (session pointers, key ids, small prefix cache).
- Fraction of requests that use warm KV (cacheable): 42% baseline; new model expected to increase cache usage to 55% due to longer context reuse patterns.
- Warm slot = an active GPU slot holding model weights + preloaded KV shards for low-latency inference (counts toward capacity).
- We assume a soft cold-start penalty that multiplies latency by 2x for cold requests; SLO budget allows 5% of requests to be cold.

Ramp scenarios (30-day window):
1) Conservative (fast): Day 0->7 rapid adoption: 0.4% of global userbase -> 3.5% by day7, 8% by day 30.
2) Nominal: steady S-curve, 0.2% day0 -> 1.5% day7 -> 6% day30.
3) Aggressive (viral): 0.8% day0 -> 6% day7 -> 18% day30.

Per-request KV delta calculation (nominal example):
- Delta tokens per request (new - baseline output) = 220 - 128 = 92 tokens.
- Extra KV bytes per request = 92 * 35 bytes = 3,220 bytes (~3.15 KB).
- If 55% of requests hit cache vs 42% baseline, incremental cache-using requests = (0.55-0.42)=13% of total requests.
- Effective avg extra KV per overall request = 3.15 KB * 0.13 = 0.41 KB (~420 bytes).

Translate to global memory pressure (nominal):
- Prod steady QPS (all models): 28,000 qps global (observed 7-day avg).
- Nominal new-model share at day30 = 6% -> new-model qps = 1,680 qps.
- New-model cache-using qps = 1,680 * 0.55 = 924 qps.
- Additional KV throughput demand from longer outputs = 924 * 3,220 bytes/sec ≈ 2.98 MB/sec (~250 GB/day).
- Steady-state additional resident KV memory estimate = approximate working set multiplier 20x of per-second influx (heuristic from prior rollouts) -> 250 GB/day * 20 ≈ 5 TB additional resident KV.

Mapping resident KV to warm slots / GPU equivalents:
- Empirical: a warm slot holds ~48 GB of useful KV shard in our sharding/layout before eviction pressure rises.
- Nominal 5 TB -> 5000 GB / 48 ≈ 104 warm slots (~equivalent GPUs if we reserve slots solely for warm).
- But cross-region distribution matters; assuming traffic split us-west1 40%, us-east1 30%, eu-west1 20%, apac-sg1 10% -> regional warm slots: us-west1 ~42, us-east1 ~31, eu-west1 ~21, apac-sg1 ~10.
- Because we already have reserved warm pool for other models (~60 slots globally), net incremental warm slots needed ~44 (rounded to 42 in earlier preview after accounting for cache eviction elasticity).

Conservative / Aggressive quick numbers (summary table):
- Conservative: extra resident KV: ~9.4 TB -> warm slots ~196 -> incremental after existing pool ~136 -> recommended immediate 2-week burst reservation + seeding.
- Nominal: extra resident KV: ~5.0 TB -> warm slots ~104 -> incremental after existing pool ~44 -> recommended pre-seed top 20% of predicted sessions (shadow seeding), monitor eviction heatmap.
- Aggressive: extra resident KV: ~15.0 TB -> warm slots ~312 -> incremental ~252 -> requires cross-region burst contracts and temporary route-level QOS.

Operational mitigations (prioritized):
1) Seeded KV shadowing: proactively route a small % (5-10%) of live traffic to a shadow fleet to warm the KV shards for predicted hot prefixes. Low-effort, very effective at lowering cold-start spike.
2) Soft quotas per org: enforce short TTLs for non-critical sessions and rate-limit heavy-key churn routes during first 14 days.
3) Dynamic model routing: temporarily route a fraction of traffic to a lightweight quantized variant for non-SLA customers to preserve warm capacity.
4) Conditional autoscale: add regional burst contracts (pre-approved capacity) for 4-week windows triggered when cached resident KV > threshold X (tunable).
5) Aggressive eviction tuning: slow down eviction/gc to avoid mass churn when new model warms — but this increases resident footprint so use carefully.

Monitoring & alarms (actionable):
- Create dashboard: resident-kv-by-region, warm-slot-usage, cold-request-rate, kv-eviction-rate, per-route-latency-p75.
- Create alerts: resident-KV > baseline + 20% (warning), > baseline + 40% (critical); cold-request-rate > 5% for 10m -> paging.
- Daily rollup report for first 14 days: day-over-day resident-KV delta, slot utilization, top 20 hot prefixes.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- We need a better working-set multiplier than 20x for long-tail workloads. Action: run a 7-day tracer using previous rollout traces (ticket JIRA-OPS-887).
- Confirm compression/packing assumption (35 bytes/token) with serving-runtime team; small changes materially alter MB/day numbers.
- Evaluate potential for partial KV offload to SSD-backed hybrid cache for eu-west1 to reduce warm slot counts.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: run quick synthetic replayer with new-model traces to validate 20x multiplier (due 2026-01-25).
- Marcus: wire resident-kv-by-region dashboard and eviction heatmap (due 2026-01-22).
- Noah: prototype seeded shadowing for top 5 prefixes in us-west1 (POC 3 days).
- SRE/Oncall: prepare escalation runbook for high cold-request-rate (due 2026-01-20).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working sheet: numbers are rounded and heuristics are conservative. Please comment with alternate multipliers, other regional splits, or additional mitigations. Link PRs or infra runbooks in linked_artifacts.

Appendix (quick math snippets):
- bytes_per_token = 35
- extra_tokens_per_req = max(0, model_out_median - baseline_out_median)
- extra_bytes_per_req = bytes_per_token * extra_tokens_per_req
- resident_kv_estimate = extra_bytes_per_req * cache_hit_fraction_new * new_model_qps * 86400s * working_set_multiplier
- warm_slots_needed = ceil(resident_kv_estimate_GB / 48)

Last checked metrics: 7-day avg global qps = 28,000 (from dashboards/production/traffic-7d), baseline resident KV = 12 TB (from kv/cluster-metrics-last-30d).

End of sheet. Keep edits tracked in doc comments.
